subject: Agriculture
title: Climate Change and New Pests
description: Learn Climate Change and New Pests in one minute.

hook.text: Every 1°C of warming lets insects eat 10–25% more crops. Warmer means hungrier—and more generations per year.

buildup.text: Cold winters kill overwintering pests. As winters warm, pest populations start the season larger.

discovery.text: Pests are moving poleward at 2.7 km per year, colonizing crops that never faced them before.

twist.text: Climate change also weakens plant defenses. Stressed plants produce fewer defensive chemicals.

climax.text: Models predict crop losses to insects could increase 50% by mid-century under current warming trends.

punchline.text: Warming feeds the pests and weakens the crops. A double hit.

quiz.question: How fast are pests expanding their range due to climate change?
